chunks: Ahmad ibn Muhammad narrated from Ali ibn al-Nu'man, from Ibn Muskhan, from Sulayman ibn Khalid, who said:

I asked Abu Abdillah (peace be upon him) about a man who cultivates another man's land, stipulating one-third for the seed and one-third for the ox. He said: 'It is not appropriate that he specify seed and ox, for it is the speech (specification) that prohibits (the contract).'

key_terms.البَذْر: Seed; the seeds used for planting.
key_terms.البَقَر: Ox/Cattle; referring to the livestock used for plowing.
key_terms.الْمُزَارَعَة: Sharecropping; a contract where one party provides land and the other labor, sharing the harvest.
key_terms.يَشْتَرِطُ: He stipulates; to specify conditions in a contract.
key_terms.يُحَرِّمُ: It prohibits/invalidates; making something forbidden or void.

ai.seo_question: What invalidates a sharecropping contract in Shia fiqh regarding seed and livestock shares?
ai.summary: In this hadith from *Tahdhib al-Ahkam*, Imam al-Sadiq (AS) clarifies that the invalidity in sharecropping (*Muzara'ah*) arises not from the share itself, but from the explicit stipulation of specific quantities for seed and livestock, which introduces uncertainty (*Gharar*). This ruling underscores the Shia juristic principle that verbal specification of inputs can void the contract, emphasizing precision in agricultural agreements to ensure fairness and avoid dispute.
